VZ.rationale: Verizon shows solid fundamental health with improving trajectory. Q1 2026 results demonstrate accelerating profitability: EPS grew +4.3% YoY to $1.20, net income +3.3% to $5.15B, and operating income expanded to $8.24B. The company achieved its first positive Q1 postpaid phone net adds since 2013 (55K), with record adjusted EBITDA of $13.4B. Management raised full-year EPS guidance to $4.95-$4.99, signaling confidence. Operating cash flow remains strong at $7.98B, supporting the 5.9% dividend yield with a ~55% payout ratio. The Frontier acquisition expands fiber passings to 25M+ homes, creating a convergence growth vector. However, the balance sheet carries significant leverage ($313B liabilities, $120B+ debt), and revenue growth is modest at ~3% YoY. Valuation is attractive: P/E of 11.2x sits at the low end of its 11-21x 12-month range, and P/B of 1.9x is near the bottom of its 1.7-2.2x window, suggesting the market is paying less for the same earnings power than it was 6-12 months ago when P/E was 16-18x. The sharp P/E compression from ~21x in early March to 11x in May reflects both earnings improvement and price adjustment, creating a value entry point. Near-term catalysts include the raised EPS guidance, ongoing transformation cost savings ($5B target), and AI-driven operational efficiencies (85% autonomous network resolution). Risks include competitive pressure from T-Mobile's broadband push, high debt levels, and rising interest rates (10Y at 4.41%). The combination of improving fundamentals, attractive valuation vs. own history, and a credible earnings upgrade catalyst supports a mildly-to-moderately positive view.
